subject: English
passage: Chemists Patricia Dubois and Atieno Kaplan have argued that brief exposure to elevated concentrations of negative air ions—charged molecules generated in abundance near turbulent water—can sharpen mental focus and thereby improve performance on tasks requiring careful reasoning. Dubois, together with Kaplan and several collaborators, claims to have found evidence for this effect in a recent study in which participants were asked to either stand for five minutes beside a cascading indoor waterfall (an environment known to produce exceptionally high negative-ion levels) or stand beside a plain interior wall in the same building. Immediately afterward, each participant was given a timed logic puzzle to solve.
prompt: Which finding from the researchers' study, if true, would most strongly support their claim?

choices.A: Participants who had stood beside the waterfall solved significantly more of the logic puzzle correctly than did participants who had stood beside the plain wall.
choices.B: Participants who solved the logic puzzle correctly used a greater number of technical terms when describing the waterfall and the wall in a postexperiment survey than did participants who did not solve the puzzle correctly.
choices.C: Participants who failed to solve the logic puzzle were significantly more likely to report feeling mentally refreshed, regardless of whether they had stood beside the waterfall or the plain wall.
choices.D: Participants who had stood beside the plain wall were significantly more likely to notice small details printed at the bottom of the puzzle page than were participants who had stood beside the waterfall.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it presents a finding that, if true, would most strongly support the researchers' claim that brief exposure to elevated negative-ion concentrations sharpens mental focus and improves performance on tasks requiring careful reasoning. According to the text, the researchers tested this effect by having participants stand beside either a cascading waterfall (a high-ion environment) or a plain interior wall and then attempt a timed logic puzzle. The finding that participants who stood beside the waterfall solved significantly more of the puzzle correctly than participants who stood beside the wall would support the researchers' claim by demonstrating that the people exposed to higher ion levels performed better on the reasoning task than the other participants did.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because a finding about participants noticing small details printed on the puzzle page would not have any bearing on the researchers' claim about reasoning performance. Being visually attentive to fine print is not the same as correctly solving a logic puzzle, so the finding would not support the idea that ion exposure improves performance on tasks requiring careful reasoning.
